paper_metadata.title: Incorporating Contexts to Open Information Extraction
paper_metadata.venue: Nanyang Technological University, Doctor of Philosophy thesis
paper_metadata.abstract: The thesis studies open information extraction (OpenIE): extracting open-form structured relational tuples from unstructured open-domain text. It develops four context-oriented contributions: DocOIE/DocIE for document-context-aware extraction; SMiLe-OIE, which fuses dependency and constituency syntax through GCNs and multi-view learning; Chunk-OIE, which uses Sentence as Chunk sequence (SaC) and chunk dependencies; and SpecTup, a semantic-and-syntactic post-processor for tuple-level speculation detection. The work frames these outputs as useful for knowledge-base/knowledge-graph construction and other downstream tasks.

problem_addressed: Improve the accuracy, contextual interpretation, efficiency, and reliability of open-domain relational-tuple extraction. The thesis identifies flexible open-form tuple representations, difficult evaluation, insufficient gold training data, sentence-only extraction, underused syntax, token-level span granularity, and speculative/non-factual tuples as central problems. It treats OpenIE tuples as candidate structured facts usable for KB/KG construction, but does not itself implement a complete knowledge-graph construction system.

methodology.description: The thesis contributes four complementary context-aware OpenIE methods. (1) DocIE: for each source sentence, concatenate neighbouring document sentences with segment embeddings; BERT bottom blocks model source-context interactions, top Transformer blocks retain source-token representations, and a CopyAttention-style LSTM decoder with attention/copying generates relational tuples. (2) SMiLe-OIE: convert dependency trees and flattened constituency trees into word-node graphs; encode BERT token representations plus relation indicators using dependency and constituency GCNs; fuse the two views using auxiliary intra-view and inter-view multi-view losses; predict BIO-style argument/relation tags for n-ary tuples. (3) Chunk-OIE: represent a sentence as a sequence of chunks (SaC), encode chunk type and chunk-level dependency structure with BERT and a dependency GCN, and learn chunking and OpenIE extraction in either two stages or end-to-end multi-task training. (4) SpecTup/OIE-Spec: after tuples are extracted, mark tuple relation tokens, encode sentence semantics with BERT, aggregate one-hop dependency neighbours of the relation using a relation-aware GCN, concatenate semantic and syntactic representations, and classify each tuple as speculative/non-speculative (optionally one of six modal classes). No entity linking, coreference resolution, canonicalization, graph fusion, or graph materialization is performed by these proposed systems.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: Open-schema extraction: OpenIE is explicitly not restricted to predefined relation/entity types or an ontology. Outputs are open-form binary or n-ary tuples. Existing KB schemas are discussed only as downstream mappings from OpenIE tuples, not as constraints used by the proposed models.

text_to_kg_stages: Text preprocessing (sentence segmentation, tokenization, POS tagging, dependency and constituency parsing, chunking)
Entity and concept extraction (open-form argument spans)
Relation and triple extraction (binary and n-ary relational tuples)
Graph validation and correction (tuple-level speculation/reliability classification)

input_output.input_type: English unstructured open-domain natural-language text: source sentences, optionally surrounding document sentences; SpecTup additionally receives an extracted relational tuple aligned to its source sentence.
input_output.input_granularity: Primarily sentence level. DocIE uses a source sentence plus a symmetric local document-context window; Chunk-OIE operates on chunks; SMiLe-OIE and SpecTup operate on tokens and parse-graph neighbourhoods. Document context is evaluated with 4–5 neighbouring sentences on each side depending on domain.
input_output.output_representation: Open-form relational tuples: binary (subject, relation, object) or n-ary (ARG0, Relation, ARG1, …, ARGn). SpecTup outputs a binary speculation label or a seven-way label (non-speculative plus six modal-auxiliary categories) for an input tuple. The thesis does not serialize or construct a complete KG.

models_and_tools: DocIE: BERT source-context encoder; top Transformer blocks; CopyAttention-style attention-and-copy LSTM decoder
SMiLe-OIE: BERT; relation indicator embedding; dependency GCN; constituency GCN; multi-view learning; BIO tagging
Chunk-OIE: BERT; SaC chunk/type embeddings; chunk-level dependency GCN; multi-task chunking/OpenIE objective
SpecTup: bert-base-uncased; tuple-relation embedding; relation-aware GCN over a dependency subgraph; softmax classifier
PyTorch 1.9.0; AllenNLP 0.9.0; spaCy and spaCy-transformers; Stanford CoreNLP
datasets: DocOIE: 800 expert-annotated source sentences from 80 documents in Healthcare and Transportation; 2,122 relational tuples; used to evaluate document-context-aware extraction
DocOIE pseudo-label training corpus: tuples generated by ReVerb, OpenIE4, and their fallback combinations
LSOIE Wiki and Science: QA-SRL 2.0-derived n-ary OpenIE data; used for SMiLe-OIE, Chunk-OIE, and SpecTup
CaRB: crowdsourced binary OpenIE benchmark; used for testing
BenchIE: fact-synset OpenIE benchmark; used for Chunk-OIE evaluation
CoNLL-2000 and OIA v1.1: chunking data used to train/evaluate SaC chunking

metrics: OpenIE: precision, recall, F1, and area under the precision-recall curve (AUC)
LSOIE evaluation in SMiLe-OIE: exact tuple matching of relations and arguments; CaRB: default lexical partial tuple matching
BenchIE: precision, recall, F1 against fact synsets
Chunking: exact-boundary precision/recall/F1 and exact-boundary-plus-type F1
SpecTup: macro precision/recall/F1, positive-class precision/recall/F1, and speculative-tuple recall by easy/medium/hard difficulty
baselines: DocIE: ReVerb, OpenIE4, Rev+Oie4, Oie4+Rev, CopyAttention+BERT, IMoJIE, and DocIE without top Transformer
SMiLe-OIE: GloVe+BiLSTM, GloVe+BiLSTM+CRF, BERT, CopyAttention, IMoJIE, CIGL-OIE+IGL-CA, BERT+Dep-GCN, BERT+Const-GCN, and graph-fusion variants
Chunk-OIE: CopyAttention, IMoJIE, CIGL-OIE, BERT, BERT+Dep-GCN, SMiLe-OIE, SpanOIE, OIE@OIA, and SaC variants
SpecTup: modal-keyword and enriched-keyword matching, semantic-only BERT variants, syntactic-only full/subgraph variants, and semantic-plus-syntactic variants
evaluation.setting: Evaluation spans four related studies. DocIE evaluates document-context extraction on DocOIE Healthcare and Transportation using CaRB scoring, with context-window ablation from 1 to 6. SMiLe-OIE trains/evaluates on LSOIE Wiki/Science and tests on CaRB, using reimplementations for n-ary settings where necessary. Chunk-OIE evaluates LSOIE Wiki/Science, CaRB, and BenchIE; compares two-stage and end-to-end training, SaC choices, and ablations. SpecTup combines LSOIE Wiki and Science subsets after removing repeats: 38,823 sentences/79,128 tuples for training and 11,339/22,038 for testing; results average three random seeds.

value: DocIE with top Transformer achieved the best DocOIE results: Healthcare AUC 47.4, precision 74.4, recall 51.3, F1 60.8; Transportation AUC 38.5, precision 56.0, recall 57.5, F1 56.9. The no-top-Transformer variant was second best in both domains.

SMiLe-OIE achieved F1/AUC of 51.73/50.88 on LSOIE-Wiki, 60.51/57.22 on LSOIE-Science, and 53.76/34.92 on CaRB. It outperformed the listed baselines on both LSOIE subsets but not CIGL-OIE+IGL-CA on CaRB AUC.

Chunk-OIE variants using CoNLL or OIA simple phrases gave the strongest results across LSOIE and BenchIE. End-to-end CoNLL reached 52.8/50.5 F1/AUC on LSOIE-Wiki and 61.5/59.7 on LSOIE-Science; end-to-end OIA-SP reached BenchIE F1 27.2 (precision 42.4, recall 20.1). The reported improvements of OIA-SP and CoNLL over the token baseline were significant at p<0.01.

SpecTup achieved macro P/R/F1 80.7/77.5/79.0 and speculative-positive P/R/F1 66.9/58.9/62.6; it had recall 100.0/67.2/40.9 for easy/medium/hard speculative cases. The authors state it outperformed all reported baselines, while noting substantial room for improvement in positive-class F1.

value: Author-reported: document context improved OpenIE over all tested sentence-level systems on two domain-specific DocOIE evaluations.
Author-reported: SMiLe-OIE integrates complementary dependency and constituency syntax; both syntax types and their multi-view fusion improved results in ablations and comparisons.

Author-reported: Chunk-OIE uses a simpler chunk-level representation yet achieved strong or state-of-the-art results on several OpenIE datasets, with significant improvements over its token-level counterpart.
Author-reported: SpecTup addresses tuple-level rather than sentence-level uncertainty and substantially improves hard-case recall relative to keyword matching.

Review-level inference: the four contributions cover complementary extraction-quality concerns—discourse context, syntax, unit granularity, and factuality—so they can inform different points in a Text-to-KG pipeline rather than representing mutually exclusive KG builders.

value: Author-reported: DocIE still relies on sentence-level pseudo labels from traditional extractors, so the document-context potential is not fully realized; it also exhibits incomplete, incorrect-boundary, redundant, and grammatical tuple errors.
Author-reported: Chunk-OIE handles coordinated chunks such as “Lily and Jimmy” as one unit and consequently scores poorly on such cases; performance on CaRB is comparable rather than uniformly best.
Author-reported: SpecTup's positive speculative-class F1 is 62.6, and hard speculative cases have only 40.9 recall.

Review-level inference: because the thesis evaluates tuple extraction and tuple reliability rather than entity canonicalization, linking, fusion, or graph serialization, an additional KG-construction layer is required before its outputs become a coherent knowledge graph.
